results.project_title: Epigenetic regulation of stress-potentiated ethanol drinking
results.phr_text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE
Stress perpetuates the cycle of excessive alcohol drinking and contributes to the transition to an alcohol use
disorder (AUD). Though stress increases drinking, treatments that target stress-potentiated alcohol use are
lacking due to an incomplete understanding of the underlying mechanisms. The long-term goal of this project is
to elucidate the epigenetic mechanisms that can lead to stress-potentiated drinking as this could lead to future
treatments for patients suffering from AUD.

results.project_title: Advanced body composition imaging to improve outcomes in lung transplantation
results.phr_text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE
Measures of adipose distribution are routinely used to assess obesity-related risk in the general
population due to strong associations between visceral obesity and mortality. Despite our
extensive work similarly demonstrating that measures of adipose distribution are also
associated with pre-transplant, peri-operative, and post-transplant morbidity and mortality for
lung transplant candidates, measures of adipose distribution have not yet been integrated into
lung transplant risk assessments. Herein, we propose to establish computed tomography (CT)
scan-based metrics of adipose distribution that can be used to inform the risk assessments of
pre-transplant, peri-operative, and post-transplant risk that are used every day to make
decisions about appropriate timing for waitlisting and operative management (e.g. single vs.
bilateral lung transplant, use of extracorporeal support) in lung transplant candidates.

results.project_title: Alterations of leukocyte integrin signaling leading to diabetes and autoimmunity
results.phr_text:
Project Narrative
This genetic study focuses on type 1 diabetes mutations in the protein coding region of the human genome,
which are potential biological targets for treatment. We are generating mice and human cell lines to
understand how these mutations cause diabetes, as well as using these animals as preclinical models for
evaluating possible precision therapies. The results from this study will enable better detection, prediction,
and treatment for patients with type 1 diabetes, and may also benefit individuals with other autoimmune
disorders.

results.project_title: Foundational Biology of Glaucoma GWAS Loci
results.phr_text:
PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE:
Glaucoma is a common group of age-related neurodegenerative diseases characterized by loss of retinal
ganglion cells and their axons that carry information from the eye to the brain. Over 127 genetic risk factors for
glaucoma have been mapped to specific places in the genome, however, basic features of these loci (i.e., the
causative genes/mutations in each locus and how they affect gene activity) have not been defined, which is an
obstacle to targeting them for therapies. Our proposed studies will use a complementary set of human, mouse,
and molecular approaches to characterize the important features of three glaucoma risk factor loci by 1)
determining the glaucoma-causing gene in each locus, 2) determining the specific DNA variants in the
glaucoma-causing genes that confer risk for disease, and 3) determining how these variants alter gene
expression and biological pathways that contribute to glaucoma pathogenesis to facilitate development of new
sight-saving glaucoma therapies.

results.project_title: Anticodon Engineered tRNA for the Treatment of Hereditary Eye Disease
results.phr_text:
PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE:
Nonsense mutations are point mutations that convert an amino acid encoding codon into a premature
termination codon and collectively represent >10% of all described causes of hereditary disease in humans,
including nearly all forms of hereditary eye disease. While there has been a longstanding appreciation that
therapies promoting “readthrough” of premature termination codons might be broadly useful for treating these
diseases, finding drugs that are efficient at readthrough, without disrupting native termination codons, has
encountered many challenges. Here, we build on a different approach for readthrough that is based on
suppressor tRNA molecules, which we propose to study in the eye using multiple mouse models of eye
disease and transgenic reporter mice.

results.project_title: Role of visceral adipose tissue in frailty among patients with Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
results.phr_text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE
Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is an increasingly prevalent chronic lung disease with no available cure;
frailty affects 50% of IPF patients, and is associated with increased severity of illness in response to acute
insults, which are the most common cause of death in IPF. We identified that visceral adipose tissue is a risk
factor for frailty and propose to investigate potential mechanisms linking visceral adipose tissue and frailty, as
modifiable risk factors for morbidity and mortality in this growing patient population. Our findings may lead to
novel therapies and clinical trials evaluating the role of existing medications in the prevention and treatment of
frailty in IPF.
